docs.title: Advanced: Merge Hyperparameter Search
docs.text:
Optional grid-search of inference merge hyperparameters (--song-gap, and optionally --nms-iou) on a frozen checkpoint. Most users never need this: the defaults in run_pipeline.sh are the usual evaluation path.

Advanced / optional

Skip this page unless you are already evaluating against labeled audio and want to retune merge parameters. For detection and F-beta with stock settings, see Typical Workflows.

Each setting is scored with the same 1-minute event F-beta protocol as f_beta_score_analysis.py: filter raw detections by confidence, merge, then Hungarian 2D IoU against annotations.csv. Confidence is swept at every grid point; the reported number is the best Overall_Micro F-beta.

Learning-rate and augmentation search lives in BirdBox-Train and is also optional. Do not mix the two: freeze --nms-iou / --song-gap while training, then run this search on the winning weights.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
run_hpo.sh at the repository root is the intended way to run this search. Edit variables at the top and leave exactly one option enabled — the same interaction style as run_pipeline.sh, but this script is not part of the default pipeline.

Option A (default, cheap) reuses one raw_detections.json and only sweeps --song-gap. Option B (expensive) re-runs detect_birds.py --no-merge once per --nms-iou, then sweeps --song-gap on each dump. Detection dominates wall time; use B only when you need to search NMS.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 BirdNET-Team
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Advanced / optional: search merge hyperparameters (song_gap, nms_iou)
# on a frozen model. Everyday detect + evaluate is run_pipeline.sh
# (or .bat / .ps1). Skip unless you have labels and want to retune merge.

# Exit immediately if a command fails
set -e

# Optional: activate local virtual environment if present.
# If .venv does not exist, the script uses the current Python on PATH.
if [ -f ".venv/bin/activate" ]; then
    echo "Activating .venv"
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source ".venv/bin/activate"
fi


#### select the dataset on which inference shall be performed #####
# DATASET_NAME="Birds-With-Labels_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Western-US"
# DATASET_NAME="Hawaii_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset-subset"
DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset"


#### raw detections for Option A: the OUTPUT_PATH of run_pipeline.sh #####
RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH="results/Just-Bird"
# RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH="results/Birds-With-Labels"


#### select model #####
MODEL_PATH="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt"
# MODEL_PATH="models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt"


#### select the species mapping (according to dataset and model) #####
SPECIES_MAPPING="Just-Bird"
# SPECIES_MAPPING="Birds-With-Labels"


#### toggle single class mode (true for Just-Bird) #####
USE_SINGLE_CLS=true
# USE_SINGLE_CLS=false


#### select output path #####
OUTPUT_PATH="results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge"


#### merge-parameter grid #####
SONG_GAPS=(0.0 0.1 0.2 0.5 1.0 2.0)
NMS_IOUS=(0.5 0.6 0.7 0.8)

IOU_THRESHOLD=0.25
BETA=1.0
DETECT_CONF=0.001
DETECT_WORKERS=18
FBETA_WORKERS=9


#########################################################################
# Choose exactly one of the two options below (they are alternatives,
# not sequential steps). Detect + single F-beta stay in run_pipeline.sh.
# Freeze these merge params while training (BirdBox-Train/run_hpo.sh).
#
# Runtime: Option A reuses one raw_detections.json (no new detect).
# Option B re-runs detect_birds --no-merge once per NMS_IOUS value,
# which dominates wall time. Prefer A unless you need to search nms_iou.
#########################################################################


SINGLE_CLS_FLAG=()
if [ "${USE_SINGLE_CLS}" = true ]; then
    SINGLE_CLS_FLAG+=(--single-cls)
fi


### only enable one of the two ###
# Option A (cheap): sweep song_gap only. Reuses the existing
# detect_birds --no-merge dump (RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH/raw_detections.json).
# Does not run detection again. nms_iou is whatever that dump was built with.
echo "Option A: sweeping song_gap on existing raw detections (no new detect)..."
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py \
    --raw-detections "${RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH}" \
    --labels "datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/annotations.csv" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --song-gaps "${SONG_GAPS[@]}" \
    --iou-threshold "${IOU_THRESHOLD}" \
    --beta "${BETA}" \
    --num-workers "${FBETA_WORKERS}" \
    --no-plot \
    "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"

# Option B (expensive): sweep nms_iou and song_gap.
# nms_iou is applied inside YOLO, so detect_birds --no-merge runs once per
# NMS_IOUS value (len(NMS_IOUS) full inference passes), then song_gap is
# swept on each dump. Comment Option A if you enable this.
# echo "Option B: re-running detect once per nms_iou, then sweeping song_gap..."
# python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py \
#     --model "${MODEL_PATH}" \
#     --audio "datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/soundscape_data" \
#     --species-mapping "${SPECIES_MAPPING}" \
#     --labels "datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/annotations.csv" \
#     --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
#     --nms-ious "${NMS_IOUS[@]}" \
#     --song-gaps "${SONG_GAPS[@]}" \
#     --detect-conf "${DETECT_CONF}" \
#     --detect-workers "${DETECT_WORKERS}" \
#     --iou-threshold "${IOU_THRESHOLD}" \
#     --beta "${BETA}" \
#     --num-workers "${FBETA_WORKERS}" \
#     --no-plot \
#     "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"
# ### only enable one of the two ###


echo
echo "All tasks completed!"
echo "Merge HPO summary is in ${OUTPUT_PATH}/summary.csv"

# Option A (cheap): song_gap only, reuse an existing --no-merge dump (no new detect)
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py `
    --raw-detections results/Birds-With-Labels `
    --labels datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/annotations.csv `
    --output-path results/Birds-With-Labels/hyperopt_merge `
    --song-gaps 0.0 0.1 0.2 0.5 1.0 2.0 `
    --num-workers 9 `
    --no-plot

rem Option A (cheap): song_gap only, reuse an existing --no-merge dump (no new detect)
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py ^
    --raw-detections results/Birds-With-Labels ^
    --labels datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/annotations.csv ^
    --output-path results/Birds-With-Labels/hyperopt_merge ^
    --song-gaps 0.0 0.1 0.2 0.5 1.0 2.0 ^
    --num-workers 9 ^
    --no-plot

docs.title: What Is Searched
docs.text:
Parameter When it is applied Needs a new detect pass? --song-gap In F-beta, after filtering by confidence (filter-then-merge) No — reuse one raw_detections.json --nms-iou Inside YOLO during detect_birds.py --no-merge Yes — one raw dump per NMS value --conf Swept automatically at every grid point No

--iou-threshold (matching detections to labels) is not part of this grid. Keep it at the evaluation default (0.25) so scores stay comparable to run_pipeline.sh.

Detection is the expensive part

--song-gap is applied in F-beta on an existing dump, so many gap values are cheap. --nms-iou is applied inside YOLO, so each NMS value is a full inference pass over the testset. Option A in run_hpo.sh never re-detects. Option B runs detect len(--nms-ious) times.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --raw-detections PATH / — Yes, unless --nms-ious Existing raw detections file or results directory from detect_birds.py --no-merge. Used for a song_gap-only search. --labels PATH / — Yes Ground truth annotations.csv. Filenames are matched without extensions. --output-path PATH / results/hyperopt_merge No Root directory for per-setting F-beta runs and summary.csv. --song-gaps FLOAT [...] / 0.0 0.1 0.2 0.5 1.0 2.0 No song_gap values in seconds to evaluate. --nms-ious FLOAT [...] / unset No If set, re-run detect --no-merge once per NMS IoU (the expensive path), then sweep --song-gaps on each dump. Requires --model, --audio, and --species-mapping. Omit this to reuse one dump (Option A). --model PATH / — With --nms-ious Frozen YOLO checkpoint. --audio PATH / — With --nms-ious Audio file or directory (typically the testset soundscape_data/ folder). --species-mapping CHOICE / — With --nms-ious Just-Bird or Birds-With-Labels. Must match the model. See species mapping. --detect-conf FLOAT / 0.001 No Confidence used when re-running detect for --nms-ious. Keep low so F-beta can sweep later. --detect-workers INT / 8 No CPU workers for those detect passes. --iou-threshold FLOAT / 0.25 No IoU for matching events to labels. Use the same value as f_beta_score_analysis.py. --beta FLOAT / 1.0 No F-beta weighting. Same meaning as in F-beta analysis. --conf-range MIN MAX STEP / 0.00 1.0 0.01 No Confidence grid at each (nms_iou, song_gap) pair. --num-workers INT / 8 No Worker processes for each F-beta confidence sweep. --no-plot flag / off No Skip F-beta plots (faster; run_hpo.sh sets this). --single-cls flag / off No Collapse all species into one class. --single-cls-name STR / bird No Class name when --single-cls is set.

docs.title: Song Gaps
docs.text:
--song-gaps lists the gaps to try, and they are merged after filtering. --song-gap is applied inside F-beta: at each confidence, surviving raw boxes of the same species are merged when the gap between them is ≤ this value. That is the same filter-then-merge policy as the app and f_beta_score_analysis.py --song-gap.

Because merging happens after detect, one --no-merge dump is enough to try every gap.

docs.title: NMS IoU Values
docs.text:
--nms-ious lists the NMS IoU values to try. NMS suppresses duplicates at detect time, inside YOLO on each 3-second clip. Changing it changes which boxes are written to raw_detections.json, so the script calls detect_birds.py --no-merge once per value. That is the main compute cost of Option B: four NMS values means four full testset inference runs, before any song_gap sweep.

Relationship to --song-gap

--nms-iou removes overlapping boxes within a clip. --song-gap then stitches surviving boxes across time into songs. They are different stages; searching both is a product grid (nms × song_gap), each cell still sweeping confidence.

docs.title: Training search vs this search
docs.text:
Training hyperparameter search is a separate, optional tool in BirdBox-Train. It retrains YOLO (learning rate, mixup, …) and scores each trial with one frozen pair such as nms_iou=0.7, song_gap=0.2, so trials differ by training recipe rather than merge settings.

If you later copy a winning best.pt into models/, this page is where you can retune merge values on labeled audio. Neither search is required for ordinary detection or evaluation.

docs.text:
All files are written under --output-path. Each grid cell gets its own folder:

Open summary.csv and take the row with the highest micro_f1. Then set --nms-iou and MERGE_FLAGS=(--song-gap ...) in run_pipeline.sh to those values for the final test evaluation.

  2. Set those values in run_pipeline.sh (detect --nms-iou, MERGE_FLAGS=(--song-gap ...) for steps 2 and 3).
  3. Run the usual evaluation steps on the testset.

The following scripts show how to run inference and evaluate the results on given ground truth annoation data. They highly depend on default values for the CLI parameters. For full controll see Complete Workflow Script.

Note: The F-beta score analysis has to be run before any merging because it handles merging itself. At each confidence threshold it computes the corresponding merging individually.

Steps 2–4 use default paths under results/. Step 1 with --no-merge writes results/raw_detections.json (or results/run_N/raw_detections.json if you re-run while results/ already has outputs). Later steps follow results/.active_run and resolve raw_detections.json / simplified.csv automatically.

docs.title: Complete Workflow Script
docs.text:
The following scripts offer the most elaborate and precise way of interacting with BirdBox. They mirror the already present scripts at the repository root.

Feel free to adapt any parameter to your use-case. For a detailed description of each CLI parameter see the other sections in this chapter. There exists one for each Python file.

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 BirdNET-Team
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Default BirdBox workflow: detect birds and evaluate against labels.
# Same as run_pipeline.bat / run_pipeline.ps1 (other shells).
# Skip run_hpo.sh unless you need the advanced merge-parameter search.

# Exit immediately if a command fails
set -e

# Optional: activate local virtual environment if present.
# If .venv does not exist, the script uses the current Python on PATH.
if [ -f ".venv/bin/activate" ]; then
    echo "Activating .venv"
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source ".venv/bin/activate"
fi


#### select the dataset on which inference shall be performed #####
# Just-Bird trained on the train and test splits of every regional dataset,
# so its scores on these test sets are in-domain.
# DATASET_NAME="Birds-With-Labels_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Western-US"
# DATASET_NAME="Hawaii_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset-subset"
DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset"


#### audio folder and labels inside datasets/${DATASET_NAME} #####
AUDIO_DIR="datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/soundscape_data"
LABELS_CSV="datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/annotations.csv"


#### select model #####
MODEL_PATH="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt"
# MODEL_PATH="models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt"


#### select the species mapping (according to dataset and model) #####
SPECIES_MAPPING="Just-Bird"
# SPECIES_MAPPING="Birds-With-Labels"


#### toggle single class mode (true for Just-Bird) #####
USE_SINGLE_CLS=true
# USE_SINGLE_CLS=false


#### select output path #####
OUTPUT_PATH="results/Just-Bird"
# OUTPUT_PATH="results/Birds-With-Labels"


#########################################################################
# The most important parameters are already set via the script variables.
# But details like IoU threshold, 
# merge settings, etc. can be changed below this heading.
# To skip entire steps (for instance the confusion matrix) 
# just uncomment the respective lines.
#########################################################################


SINGLE_CLS_FLAG=()
if [ "${USE_SINGLE_CLS}" = true ]; then
    SINGLE_CLS_FLAG+=(--single-cls)
fi

# Merge settings for steps 2 and 3. Empty keeps the model's defaults:
# window fusion with a 0.05 s phrase gap for Just-Bird, the song merge with a
# 0.1 s gap for Birds-With-Labels.
MERGE_FLAGS=()
# MERGE_FLAGS=(--phrase-gap 0)    # window fusion: one box per call
# MERGE_FLAGS=(--phrase-gap 0.3)  # window fusion: longer phrase boxes
# MERGE_FLAGS=(--song-gap 0.2)    # song merge: join songs across longer pauses

# Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and

# This matches the filter-then-merge policy when 
# later filtering at each confidence threshold.
echo "Running inference (raw detections, no merge)..."
python src/inference/detect_birds.py \
    --audio "${AUDIO_DIR}" \
    --model "${MODEL_PATH}" \
    --species-mapping "${SPECIES_MAPPING}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --output-format json-with-algorithm-metadata \
    --conf 0.001 \
    --no-merge \
    --nms-iou 0.8 \
    --num-workers 4


# Step 2: F-beta analysis on raw detections: 
# at each confidence threshold we filter then merge.
echo "Running F-beta score analysis (filter-then-merge per threshold)..."
python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py \
    --raw-detections "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --labels "${LABELS_CSV}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}/f_1.0_score_analysis" \
    --beta 1.0 \
    --iou-threshold 0.25 \
    "${MERGE_FLAGS[@]}" \
    --num-workers 8 \
    "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"


# Step 3: From raw detections, filter at the model's default confidence
# (0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.2 for Birds-With-Labels; add --conf to change it) and merge.
echo "Filtering raw detections at the model's default confidence and merging for confusion matrix..."
python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py \
    --raw-detections "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --output-format all \
    "${MERGE_FLAGS[@]}"


# Step 4: Run confusion matrix analysis.
echo "Running confusion matrix analysis..."
python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py \
    --detections "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --labels "${LABELS_CSV}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}/confusion_matrix_analysis" \
    --iou-threshold 0.25 \
    "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"


# Step 5: Examine results in results/ directory
echo
echo "All tasks completed!"
echo "Results can now be examined in the ${OUTPUT_PATH} directory."

docs.title: Ground-Truth Labels
docs.text:
Evaluation expects ground truth as a comma-separated CSV with a fixed header row. The layout matches the annotations.csv files from the utilized Zenodo Datasets listed in Available Models and Respective Datasets.

f_beta_score_analysis.py and confusion_matrix_analysis.py read this format with pandas.read_csv and require the exact column names below.

docs.title: Header (required, exact spelling)
docs.text: Filename,Start Time (s),End Time (s),Low Freq (Hz),High Freq (Hz),Species eBird Code

docs.title: Column Reference
docs.text:
Column Type Required? Description Filename string Yes Base recording name as stored on disk (e.g. SNE_001_17.wav). Used to match detections. See Filename matching. Start Time (s) float Yes Interval start in seconds from the beginning of that file. End Time (s) float Yes Interval end in seconds (must be ≥ start). Low Freq (Hz) integer Yes Lower frequency bound of the annotation box in Hz. High Freq (Hz) integer Yes Upper frequency bound in Hz. Species eBird Code string Yes Cornell/Clements eBird species code (e.g. herthr, amerob, cangoo).

There is no confidence column in ground truth. Inference CSV may add a seventh Confidence column. See Detection Output Formats for that format.

docs.title: Example Rows
docs.text:
From the Western-US test set:

Filename,Start Time (s),End Time (s),Low Freq (Hz),High Freq (Hz),Species eBird Code
SNE_001_17.wav,3.8,5.9,3219,4804,herthr
SNE_001_17.wav,0.0,7.6,2666,5405,herthr
SNE_001_17.wav,0.0,7.7,1297,4564,amerob

From the Northeastern-US test set:

Filename,Start Time (s),End Time (s),Low Freq (Hz),High Freq (Hz),Species eBird Code
SSW_001_0.wav,47.4,51.3,0,2647,cangoo
SSW_001_2.wav,0.0,0.6,0,4509,cangoo

Unknown or placeholder species codes

Some rows use placeholder codes such as ???? when the annotator could not assign a species. They are loaded as literal strings. Matching still runs, but metrics for that code may be meaningless unless detections use the same token.

docs.title: Filename matching
docs.text:
Matching pairs detections to labels per recording, using only the filename stem (path and extension stripped):

Label file Detection file Matched key SNE_001_17.wav SNE_001_17.flac SNE_001_17 SSW_001_0.wav SSW_001_0.wav SSW_001_0

Filename matching rules

  • The basename in Filename must agree between labels and detections after normalization.
  • Different extensions between label CSV and detection export are fine.
  • Different paths on disk do not matter—only the Filename column value.

docs.title: Creating your own labels
docs.text:
1. Copy the header line exactly (including spaces and parentheses).
  2. Use seconds and Hz consistent with your audio length and spectrogram view.
  3. Put the same Filename values you expect in detection outputs (typically the audio basename).
  4. Use eBird codes that exist in your model's species mapping.

Raven or other tools can be adapted if you export or convert to this six-column layout.

For CLI usage and invocation examples for each tool that reads this file, see f-beta-score-analysis and confusion-matrix-analysis.

docs.title: Audio and Model Inputs
docs.text: BirdBox reads field recordings and a trained YOLO weights file, then maps neural-network class IDs to species using a named mapping in src/config.py. This page documents the accepted formats for the --audio, --model, and --species-mapping inputs. For CLI flags, defaults, and invocation examples see the detect-birds reference.

docs.title: Audio inputs
docs.text: --audio may be a single file or a directory. Directories are searched recursively for supported files.

docs.title: Supported extensions
docs.text:
Extension Recommended? Notes .wav Yes Lossless. Matches training data best. .flac Yes Lossless. Fully supported. .ogg Use with care Lossy. May reduce recall on faint or high-frequency calls. .mp3 Use with care Lossy. Same caveat as OGG.

Case is ignored (.WAV and .wav are both found).

docs.title: Processing behavior
docs.text:
• Mono conversion: Stereo recordings are collapsed to mono before spectrogram generation.
  • Arbitrary length: Clips are processed in overlapping windows.
  • Batch mode: Point --audio at a folder to process every supported file under it in one run.

Lossy audio formats

MP3 and OGG are supported via soundfile, but the models were trained on lossless WAV. In a study of avian recordings, MP3 compression reduced the detections of human listeners and automated recognisers [19]. If detections look weak on a compressed file, re-run the same recording as WAV or FLAC before tuning thresholds.

docs.title: Model files
docs.text:
--model must point to a YOLO-compatible weights file loaded by Ultralytics. BirdBox supports four formats:

Format Typical use Runtime .pt PyTorch checkpoint. Default for BirdBox releases. PyTorch (CUDA or CPU) .onnx Cross-platform deployment. Quantized variants available. ONNX Runtime (GPU or CPU) .tflite Edge devices and mobile targets. LiteRT / ai-edge-litert (CPU) .engine Maximum throughput on NVIDIA GPUs. TensorRT (NVIDIA GPU required)

Pretrained releases on TUC-Cloud ship as .pt. Custom models can be trained with BirdBox-Train.

Each format requires its own Python environment. Install the correct runtime before switching formats.

Environment must match the model format

Loading a .tflite, .onnx, or .engine model from a .pt environment will fail with an import error or silently produce incorrect results. Run python install.py --model-format <FORMAT> to set up the right environment. See Install Parameters for the full format-to-runtime table.

Format parity

Detection quality of the .onnx and .tflite formats is validated by running inference on the same audio and comparing results against the .pt baseline. See Just-Bird format parity and Birds-With-Labels format parity for the current scores.

Platform restrictions

.engine files are compiled for a specific GPU architecture and TensorRT version. A model built on one card may not run on a different GPU generation, and it only loads in the TensorRT version that built it. Pass --model-format engine during installation to set up the pinned TensorRT runtime.

docs.title: Species Mapping
docs.text:
The --species-mapping name must match the label space the model was trained on. It is not inferred from the weights filename. You pass it explicitly. For specific mappings see Species Mapping.

Allowed values for the species-mapping parameter:

Value Region / role Just-Bird Binary bird vs. background Birds-With-Labels Species-level model for all five regions

Each key resolves to id_to_ebird, ebird_to_name, and display colors in src/config.py. The mapping name is stored in detection JSON as model_config.species_mapping.

Mapping must match the model

If --species-mapping does not match the model's training conf.yaml / class list, outputs will carry wrong eBird codes with no error. Always pair model file and mapping from the same release (e.g. Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt with Birds-With-Labels).

docs.title: File Flows
docs.text: BirdBox moves data through a small set of well-defined file types: audio and models go in, detections and evaluation artifacts come out. This section is the schema contract for pipeline scripts, external tools, and anyone wiring BirdBox into a larger workflow.

docs.title: File Flow for Detection Only
docs.text:
For field use or exporting annotations. No ground-truth CSV and no evaluation scripts. You run inference once at a chosen --conf. Song merging happens inside detect_birds.py unless you pass --no-merge.

    audio[Audio WAV/FLAC/OGG/MP3]
    model[YOLO model .pt / .onnx / .engine]

  model --> detect
  mapping --> detect
  detect --> outJSON

Use --output-format all to write every format in one run, or pick a single format. Details are on Detection Output Formats in this section.

For benchmarking on a labeled test set. Run detection once at very low confidence with --no-merge, tune threshold utilizing annotations.csv, then filter + merge and score errors. This matches run_pipeline.sh at the repository root.

docs.title: Detection Output Formats
docs.text:
BirdBox can write inference results in four interchange formats. The same choices apply to detect_birds and filter_and_merge_detections. Both accept --output-format as a space-separated list or all.

Both commands take --output-path as an output directory. Each format writes a fixed, descriptive filename inside that directory.

detect_birds.py also writes args.yaml in that directory. It stores every CLI argument for the run so later inference folders can be compared. The evaluation scripts write their own args.yaml inside their result folders (for example results/f_beta_score_analysis/ and results/confusion_matrix_analysis/).

Re-threshold without re-inference via filter_and_merge_detections. Archival output with full model_config. The evaluation pipeline reads raw_detections.json only. simplified-csv simplified.csv Confusion matrix analysis. docs.title: 1. json-with-algorithm-metadata
docs.text:
Filename: with_algorithm_metadata.json or raw_detections.json depending on --no-merge parameter.

Includes the detections as well as algorithm specific metadata such as nms iou threshold, average confidence, max confidence and so on.

docs.title: Top-level structure
docs.text:
{
  "audio_file": "/path/to/recording.wav",
  "model_config": {
    "model": "models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt",
    "confidence_threshold": 0.2,
    "nms_iou_threshold": 0.7,
    "song_gap_threshold": 0.1,
    "species_mapping": "Birds-With-Labels"
  },
  "detection_count": 12,
  "detections": [ /* see field tables below */ ]
}

In batch mode (directory input), audio_file is replaced by "audio_files": [...] and "file_count": N. After filter_and_merge_detections, model_config is kept and a filtering_config block is added:

{
  "filtering_config": { "confidence_threshold": 0.25, "song_gap_threshold": 0.1 },
  "original_detection_count": 1842,
  "detection_count": 87,
  "detections": [ /* merged song segments */ ]
}

Raw vs merged in evaluation

f_beta_score_analysis.py reads raw JSON and re-applies filter-then-merge per confidence threshold. confusion_matrix_analysis.py expects merged intervals in simplified CSV, not this JSON.

Filename: xeno-canto-annota.json

Exports a lean Annota-JSON payload for Xeno-Canto. BirdBox uses Cornell/Clements eBird codes internally. Xeno-Canto expects AviList scientific names in this format, see Taxonomy conversion.

The set-level envelope contains provenance fields and fixed BirdBox identifiers. Fields like set_uri, set_creator_id, set_owner, set_license, funding, and project_uri are left empty. Export-only XC fields (original_set_metadata, annotation_xc_id, etc.) are stripped before write.

docs.title: Taxonomy conversion (eBird → AviList)
docs.text:
BirdNET-family training data uses eBird/Clements 2021 codes. Annota-JSON expects AviList scientific names. BirdBox bridges this with:

  1. taxonomies/Cornell-to-AviList-mapping.json — lowercase eBird code → scientific_name and english_name.
  2. Fallback order in build_xeno_canto_json:
  3. AviList mapping entry
  4. detection scientific_name if already set
  5. ebird_to_name from the active species mapping (scientific part before _)
  6. raw eBird code string

Split/merge caveats and how the mapping file is generated are documented in taxonomies/README.md in the repository.

Filter-and-merge export reads model_config.species_mapping from the input JSON when present.

docs.title: Algorithm Overview
docs.text:
This section describes the algorithmic ideas and the concepts utilized within BirdBox during inference.

For user-facing parameters see CLI Reference or API Reference. To compare different models, take a look at Models and Metrics. If you are interested in the file flow see File Flows.

docs.title: Inference Algorithm Concept
docs.text:
The key idea of the BirdBox inference is to use YOLO[23] from Ultralytics[9] with a sliding window approach. Both BirdBox models are YOLO11 object detectors: Just-Bird (YOLO11s, one bird class) and Birds-With-Labels (YOLO11l, 632 species and an unknown class). YOLO cannot run on continuous audio, so the recording is cut into short, overlapping images:

  1. Load the audio. It is mixed to mono and resampled to 32 kHz. Silence is added at the end so that the last 3 s window is complete; boxes in that silence are cut at the real end of the file.
  2. Compute a log-floor mel spectrogram with STFT[1]: log power minus each band's noise floor, one minute at a time to bound the memory. It does not change with the recording level (details).
  3. Cut 3 s clips every 1.5 s (50% overlap) and render each as a 256×256 pixel image. BirdNET analyzes audio in 3 s segments as well [10].
  4. Run YOLO on the clips in batches. Boxes below the confidence threshold are dropped (default 0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.2 for Birds-With-Labels), and overlapping boxes within a clip are reduced by non-maximum suppression [8] (--nms-iou, default 0.7).
  5. Convert the boxes from pixels to seconds and Hz. The frequency axis follows the HTK mel scale from 50 Hz to 15 kHz, the inverse of how the training labels were drawn.
  6. Merge the boxes of overlapping windows into one set of detections per file, with window fusion (Just-Bird) or the song merge (Birds-With-Labels), see below.
  7. Write the detections in the selected output formats.

To examine the generation of the spectrograms in detail, see Spectrogram Generation. The various output data formats provided by BirdBox can be examined in Detection Output Formats.

docs.title: Merging the Windows
docs.text:
Consecutive windows overlap by half, so almost every call is seen by two windows. Any vocalization of 1.5 s or less lies completely inside at least one window; only longer vocalizations can be cut into parts. The two views of a call rarely give exactly the same box, and the merge decides what is kept. BirdBox has two merges, and each model has its default (--merge overrides it).

The figure shows both merges on six seconds of the demo sample. The song merge unions the two views of a call and joins calls less than 0.1 s apart, so the two calls at 9.5–10.1 s become one box. Window fusion keeps one box for each of them.

docs.title: Window Fusion (Just-Bird)
docs.text:
Window fusion keeps one box per call, or per phrase with a phrase gap. It works in four steps. The figure below shows each step on another six seconds of the demo sample. Solid boxes are what a step keeps, and dashed boxes what it removes or merges into others.

  1. Ownership. Each window owns its middle half (the thick lines at the top). The first window also owns the start of the file, the last one the end. A box is kept only from the window that owns its centre, which is the window that sees the call most centrally. The middle halves tile the file, so every call is kept once. The calls at 43.8 and 44.2 s were boxed by both windows, and only the boxes of the window that owns them stay. A call that only the other window found is lost: the faint call at 44.7 s and 2.5–4.5 kHz was boxed only by a window whose middle half ends at 44.25 s.
  2. Weighted box fusion. YOLO's non-maximum suppression within a window leaves boxes that overlap less than IoU 0.7. Boxes of one window that overlap at 2D IoU ≥ 0.4 are averaged, weighted by confidence [27], and keep the strongest confidence. At 47.2–49.5 s two boxes of one window become one.
  3. Drop nested boxes. A box that lies at least 80% inside a larger box is removed, for example a syllable inside the box of its whole call. At 46.3–47.2 s the box of the first call goes, because it lies inside the longer box that starts with it. The step keeps the larger box even when it is the less confident one. Nested boxes are dropped before the join, so a removed box cannot change a joined box later. This removes 10–25% of the boxes without lowering F1.
  4. Join. Boxes in the same frequency band (frequency IoU ≥ 0.8) that overlap in time by at least 0.05 s are linked, for example a long call that two windows cut differently. Every group of linked boxes becomes one box, and this repeats on the joined boxes until nothing joins. With a phrase gap above 0, boxes closer than the gap are linked instead, so syllables become phrase boxes. Just-Bird uses 0.05 s by default; --phrase-gap 0 keeps one box per call. In the figure the boxes from 46.3 s on become one phrase box, which continues to 62.4 s, and the boxes before 43 s become one.

On test sets labelled per call, fusion raised micro F1 at IoU 0.5 over the song merge, from 0.515 to 0.582 on Hawai'i and from 0.615 to 0.637 on Southern Sierra Nevada (models trained on each dataset alone). For the flags, see Merge Method.

docs.title: Phrase Gap
docs.text:
Some datasets box every syllable, others one box per phrase or song. The phrase gap sets how far apart boxes in one band may be and still be joined. Only this time rule changes with the gap, so the boxes change gradually as it grows. Just-Bird defaults to 0.05 s because it is run on recordings of any convention.

Each point is the best F1 over all thresholds on full recordings, and the y-axes differ between panels. The first two panels use the Just-Bird recipe trained without Southern Sierra Nevada, and the third the released models on validation minutes they did not train on.

On call labels the score falls steadily as the gap grows, while on phrase and song labels it barely moves. The 0.05 s default costs 0.005 on Hawai'i and adds at most 0.005 on the other two sets. The current model (November 2026) is well ahead on song labels at every gap, because it draws phrase boxes where its training labels did. For the values to pass, see Phrase Gap.

docs.title: Song Merge (Birds-With-Labels)
docs.text:
The song merge joins detections of the same species whose gap is at most the song gap (--song-gap, default 0.1 s) into one song box that spans all of them. Most of the Birds-With-Labels training labels box whole songs, and the wide song boxes match them better than single calls (fusion scored 0.02–0.05 lower). For Just-Bird (--merge reconstruct), boxes are only joined if they also share the frequency band, so calls of different birds are not chained.

For details, see Song Gap Threshold.

docs.title: Filter, Then Merge
docs.text: The confidence threshold is applied to the raw boxes of each window, before merging. The evaluation tools work the same way: detect_birds.py --no-merge writes the raw boxes once, and F-beta analysis or Filter and Merge Detections filter them at any threshold and merge them as detection would.

docs.text:
[1] Allen, J. B., & Rabiner, L. R. (1977). "A unified approach to short-time Fourier analysis and synthesis." Proceedings of the IEEE, 65(11), 1558–1564.

[8] Hosang, J., Benenson, R., & Schiele, B. (2017). "Learning non-maximum suppression." Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 4507–4515.

[9] Jocher, G., & Qiu, J. (2024). Ultralytics YOLO11 (Version 11.0.0) [Computer software]. AGPL-3.0. https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics. There is no YOLO11 paper; this is the citation given in the YOLO11 documentation.

[10] Kahl, S., Wood, C. M., Eibl, M., & Klinck, H. (2021). "BirdNET: A deep learning solution for avian diversity monitoring." Ecological Informatics, 61:101236.

[23] Redmon, J., et al. (2016). "You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection.“ Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR).

[27] Solovyev, R., Wang, W., & Gabruseva, T. (2021). "Weighted boxes fusion: Ensembling boxes from different object detection models." Image and Vision Computing, 104117.

docs.title: Spectrogram Generation
docs.text:
BirdBox converts raw audio into log-floor mel spectrograms before running YOLO detection: log power in decibels minus each frequency band's noise floor. This page documents the complete preprocessing pipeline. Following these steps exactly lets you reproduce the same spectrogram representation used during both training and inference.

For the full implementation details, you can have a look at pcen_inference.py.

docs.title: Pipeline at a Glance
docs.text:
The pipeline runs in six sequential stages:

  1. Load and normalize audio to a common amplitude range
  2. Resample to 32,000 Hz, pad the end and split the audio into one-minute segments
  3. Compute the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT)
  4. Apply a mel filterbank to compress frequency bins
  5. Convert to decibels and subtract each band's noise floor (log-floor)
  6. Extract fixed-length clips and render them as 256×256 pixel images

Stages 3 to 6 run once per segment. Each step is described in detail below, including all parameter values.

docs.title: Stage 1: Audio Loading and Normalization
docs.text:
BirdBox reads audio using soundfile, with a librosa fallback for problematic files. Stereo recordings are mixed down to mono by averaging both channels.

The amplitude is then scaled to the integer range before any spectral processing:

audio = (audio * (2 ** 31)).astype("float32")

This maps the normalized float input, typically in [-1.0, 1.0], into the range of a 32-bit signed integer. The scaling is kept from the training pipeline. Log-floor itself does not depend on it: any constant factor cancels when the noise floor is subtracted.

docs.title: Stage 2: Resampling, End Padding and Segments
docs.text:
All audio is resampled to a fixed sample rate using librosa.resample. Files already at the target rate are passed through without modification.

The clips start every 1.5 s. If the file does not end on that grid, or is shorter than 3 s, silence is added at the end until the last clip is complete. Boxes that the model finds in this silence are cut at the real end of the file, and boxes that start after it are dropped.

The spectrogram is not computed for the whole file at once. To bound the memory, the audio is split into one-minute segments. Each segment is computed with 2 s of the neighbouring audio before and after it, so a clip that starts near the end of a segment is still complete. Each clip is taken from the segment in which it starts. Segments are independent, so for a single file --num-workers computes them in parallel (for several files it processes the files in parallel).

Parameter Value Target sample rate 32,000 Hz Segment length 60 s Context before and after a segment 2 s End padding silence up to the end of the last 3 s clip

docs.title: Stage 3: Short-Time Fourier Transform
docs.text:
The STFT is computed using librosa.stft[20] with the following parameters. Note that the window length equals the FFT size to avoid zero-padding artifacts inside the analysis window.

Parameter Value Notes n_fft 2048 FFT size; sets frequency resolution win_length 2048 Equals n_fft; no zero-padding inside window hop_length 375 Frame step in samples (~11.72 ms per frame) window "flattop" Flat-top window for accurate amplitude representation center False No edge-padding; frames start at sample 0

The power spectrogram is derived from the complex STFT output:

stft = librosa.stft(audio, n_fft=2048, win_length=2048,
                    hop_length=375, window="flattop", center=False)
abs2_stft = np.abs(stft) ** 2

docs.title: Why flat-top?
docs.text: A flat-top window has a very flat passband in the frequency domain. This minimizes amplitude error for tonal signals, which is important for accurately representing bird vocalizations that may be near bin boundaries. This error between bins is known as scalloping loss [5], and flat-top windows are designed to keep it small [6].

docs.title: Stage 4: Mel Filterbank
docs.text:
The power spectrogram is mapped onto a mel-scale filterbank using librosa.feature.melspectrogram. BirdBox uses the HTK mel formula throughout, consistent with both training and inference.

Parameter Value Notes n_mels 256 Number of mel bands (output height) fmin 50 Hz Lowest frequency included fmax 15,000 Hz Highest frequency included htk True Uses the HTK formula, not the Slaney formula 
melspec = librosa.feature.melspectrogram(
    S=abs2_stft, sr=32000, n_fft=2048,
    n_mels=256, fmin=50, fmax=15000, htk=True
)

Frequency Range

The 50–15,000 Hz range covers the vast majority of bird vocalizations while discarding low-frequency rumble and ultrasonic content above the range of interest. The HTK formula spaces mel bands differently than the Slaney formula. Using the wrong formula at inference will produce mismatched filterbanks and degrade detection performance.

docs.title: Stage 5: Log-Floor Normalization
docs.text:
The mel power is converted to decibels, and each mel band's noise floor is subtracted: the 20th percentile of that band's levels over the segment. The image therefore shows how far each sound rises above the background of its own band. Values from 3 dB below to 45 dB above the floor fill the colour range (0 to 100 on the image scale); louder sounds take the brightest colour.

db = 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(melspec, 1e-10))
sound = melspec.sum(axis=0) > 0                    # leave out digital silence
floor = np.percentile(db[:, sound], 20, axis=1, keepdims=True)
features = (db - floor + 3.0) * (100.0 / 48.0)    # -3..45 dB above the floor -> 0..100
Parameter Value Role Floor percentile 20 The background level of each band over the segment Floor window the segment (60 s plus 2 s of context on each side) One floor per band and segment Lowest colour 3 dB below the floor Quiet background stays dark but visible Brightest colour 45 dB above the floor Nearly no call reaches it (less than 0.15% of the pixels inside labelled calls) Digital silence left out of the floor The padding at the end of a file does not pull the floor down

What it gives. A recorder's gain adds the same number of decibels to every band and cancels when the floor is subtracted, so the same scene gives the same image whatever the recording level. A loud sound barely moves a 20th percentile, so the quiet tail after a loud call stays visible.

Why not PCEN. BirdBox used Per-Channel Energy Normalization (PCEN) until November 2026. PCEN was introduced for keyword spotting [29]; on recordings of natural environments it brings the distribution of magnitudes close to a Gaussian and decorrelates the frequency bands [16], and for bird flight calls it reduced overfitting to the time of day [17]. With BirdBox's settings it kept about a quarter of the recording level in the image, so a model learned the level of its training recordings: with the Southern Sierra Nevada recordings played 12 dB louder, recall dropped from 0.53 to 0.38, and with the Hawai'i recordings 12 dB quieter it made many more faint false alarms. Its 1 s smoother also dimmed the quiet tail after a loud onset. Log-floor matched or beat PCEN on a site the models never saw, and its output does not change with the recording level (results in the BirdBox-Train repository, holdout_ssn/RESULTS.md).

docs.title: Warm-up Frames and Left Pad
docs.text:
Two steps from the PCEN pipeline are kept, because the models were trained with them. The first frames of the mel spectrogram (up to 100) are repeated in front of it, and the first 0.5 s of the segment audio is copied in front of it before the STFT. Both enter the floor percentile and are dropped afterwards:

segment_with_pad = np.concatenate([segment_audio[:16000], segment_audio])  # before the STFT
loop_length = min(100, melspec.shape[1] // 4)
melspec_looped = np.concatenate([melspec[:, :loop_length], melspec], axis=1)
features = log_floor(melspec_looped)[:, loop_length:]
features = features[:, int(0.5 * 32000) // 375:]  # drop the 42 pad frames
Parameter Value Repeated frames min(100, frames // 4) left_pad_length 0.5 s (16,000 samples at 32 kHz) Pad frames dropped afterwards 42 (16,000 // 375)

docs.title: Stage 6: Clip Extraction and Image Rendering
Clip Parameters
docs.text:
Fixed-length clips are extracted from the log-floor output using a sliding window with 50% overlap. Each clip covers exactly 3 seconds of audio.

Parameter Value Clip length 3 s (252 frames) Clip hop 1.5 s (50% overlap) Output shape per clip 256 × 252 (mel bands × time frames)

The 252-frame clip length follows from the hop length: 252 × 375 / 32,000 ≈ 2.953 s, which BirdBox rounds to 3 seconds.

docs.title: Image Rendering
docs.text:

)

The vmin and vmax values are baked into the model's training distribution. Using a different colormap or rescaling will shift pixel intensities relative to what the YOLO model was trained on, causing unpredictable detection results.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This section provides information for typical mistakes one can make when interacting with BirdBox.

docs.title: No Detections
docs.text:
If BirdBox returns an empty results file, the most common cause is a model/mapping mismatch or a threshold that is set too high for exploratory work.

  • Verify that --model and --species-mapping belong together: Just-Bird for Just-Bird_fp32.pt, Birds-With-Labels for Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt (files from before 28 October 2026 may still be called All-In-One.pt).
  • Lower the confidence threshold for exploratory runs. The defaults are 0.15 for Just-Bird and 0.2 for Birds-With-Labels. Try --conf 0.1, or --conf 0.001 to capture every raw hit.
  • Check audio format and quality. WAV and FLAC outperform lossy formats such as MP3 and OGG for faint or distant calls. In a study of avian recordings, MP3 compression reduced the detections of human listeners and automated recognisers [19].
  • Confirm that the audio file actually covers the time ranges recorded in your labels when running an evaluation.

Quick sanity check

Run BirdBox on a short clip you know contains a loud, clear call. If that also returns nothing, the issue is almost certainly the model/mapping pair, not the audio.

docs.title: Too Many False Positives
docs.text:
False positives usually indicate that the confidence threshold is too permissive or that overlapping detections are being merged incorrectly.

  • Increase --conf to raise the detection bar. Even a small step (e.g., 0.3 to 0.5) can cut noise significantly.
  • Tune --nms-iou to control how aggressively duplicate bounding boxes within a window are suppressed.
  • Run confusion_matrix_analysis.py and inspect the background row and column to distinguish species confusion from generic noise hits.

docs.title: Boxes Too Long or Too Short
docs.text:
Box length depends on the merge (see Merging the Windows) and should match how your labels are drawn.

  • Just-Bird boxes single syllables, but your labels box phrases or songs: raise --phrase-gap (default 0.05 s, try 0.1 to 0.5) so nearby syllables in the same band are joined.
  • Just-Bird joins calls that your labels keep apart: pass --phrase-gap 0 for one box per call.
  • Birds-With-Labels joins unrelated calls into one long song box: reduce --song-gap (default 0.1 s). Raise it to join songs across longer pauses.

docs.title: Recording in the Demo Is Silent
docs.text: The Demo warns while recording when no sound arrives from the microphone for 1.5 s, and shows the input level under the timer. If the warning appears, check that the microphone is not muted, turned all the way down, or blocked for the browser in the system settings.

docs.title: Memory or Runtime Issues
docs.text:
Large audio collections can put pressure on RAM or stretch runtimes. Process smarter before scaling up hardware.

  • Reduce parallelism by lowering --num-workers for inference and F-beta analysis.
  • Process subsets of files and merge the resulting reports afterwards rather than running everything in one pass.
  • Prefer GPU-backed runs for large jobs when a compatible device is available.

Avoid redundant inference

Generate the raw detections JSON once using --no-merge. Re-running full inference just to experiment with confidence thresholds wastes significant time on large datasets.

docs.title: Filename Mismatch in Evaluation
docs.text:
Evaluation tools match audio files against labels using the normalized stem, which is the base filename with the extension stripped. If stems do not match, the file is silently skipped.

Audio file Label file Result recording_01.wav recording_01.flac Match siteA_recording_01.wav recording_01.flac No match

How to fix a mismatch

Inspect both the filename fields in your detection CSV or JSON and the filenames in your labels CSV. Unify the base names in one of the two sources, then re-run metrics.

docs.title: Birds-With-Labels Model Types and Format Parity
docs.text: BirdBox ships two pretrained models, Just-Bird and Birds-With-Labels. Both are released in multiple runtime formats to cover different deployment targets. This page covers the Birds-With-Labels model. It documents every available format and shows how each one compares against the PyTorch baseline on identical recordings, so you can confirm that conversion or quantization does not degrade detection quality.

docs.title: Supported model formats
docs.text:
Each format targets a different deployment scenario. Install the matching runtime with python install.py --model-format <FORMAT>. See Installation for the full setup guide.

Format Typical use case Runtime .pt Default. PyTorch checkpoint, easiest to get started. PyTorch (CUDA or CPU) .onnx Cross-platform deployment, quantized variants available. ONNX Runtime (GPU or CPU) .tflite Edge devices and mobile targets. LiteRT / ai-edge-litert (CPU) .engine Maximum throughput on NVIDIA GPUs. TensorRT (NVIDIA GPU required)

Platform restrictions

.engine files are compiled for a specific GPU architecture. A model built on one card may not run on a different GPU generation.

Each format requires its own Python environment

Do not load a .tflite, .onnx, or .engine model from a .pt environment. The wrong environment will either raise an import error immediately or silently degrade results. Run python install.py --model-format <FORMAT> to install the correct runtime before switching formats. See Install Parameters for the full table.

docs.title: Verdict criteria
docs.text:
PASS

The model matches at least 90% of baseline detections, adds no more than 10% extra detections, and keeps the mean confidence difference at or below 0.05. The export is safe to use in place of the baseline.

WARN

One or more thresholds were exceeded. The model runs but performance may have degraded after conversion or quantization. Inspect the per-model detail below and compare detections on your own audio before deploying.

FAIL

The worker subprocess exited with an error. The model did not produce any detections. Check the per-model detail below for the full traceback.

docs.title: Metric glossary
docs.text:
Matching is one-to-one and recording by recording: a candidate detection can match a baseline detection of the same species when their 2D IoU (time and frequency) is at least 0.5. Pairs are taken in order of decreasing IoU, and each detection is used at most once.

Metric What it tells you Mean IoU Average time-and-frequency box overlap between matched pairs. 1.000 is a perfect overlap. Lower values mean boxes drifted in position or size. Mean Conf Δ Average absolute confidence difference on matched detections. Near 0.000 means the converted model is as confident as the baseline. Max Conf Δ Largest single confidence difference among matched detections. Surfaces worst-case outliers that the mean hides. Load (s) Wall-clock seconds to load the model file and build the detector. Detect (s) Wall-clock seconds spent running inference on all recordings.

The figure shows the validation mAP, the box loss and the classification loss after each epoch of training. The validation set is the val splits of all five datasets and of Bird-Sounds-Global.

The model was trained in two runs. The first ran 30 epochs from YOLO11l with a cosine learning rate. Its validation mAP peaked at epoch 15, because the learning rate fell too soon. The second run started from that epoch with the linear learning rate of the March 2026 model, which stays high for longer. The dashed line marks the change and the dotted line the kept checkpoint.

Model Checkpoint

The weights that produced the highest metrics/mAP50-95 on the validation split were selected for the final model.

Rare species appear more often in training than in the data. Each epoch repeats an image more often the rarer its rarest species is (repeat-factor sampling as in LVIS, threshold 0.001).

docs.title: Birds With Labels Model
docs.text:
The Birds-With-Labels model combines all five zenodo datasets mentioned in the introduction with Bird-Sounds-Global, annotated soundscapes from xeno-canto. The five datasets bring almost 407 hours of soundscape recordings with 155,584 bounding box labels of 281 bird species. Bird-Sounds-Global adds 111 hours with 62,030 labels of 765 species from many countries. The model has 633 classes: the 281 regional species, the 351 Bird-Sounds-Global species with at least 10 training labels in at least 3 recordings, and the unknown class ???? for the rest.

Formerly All-In-One

Until 28 October 2026 this model was called All-In-One. Files made before then still carry the old name: rename All-In-One.pt to Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt and pass --species-mapping Birds-With-Labels. BirdBox no longer accepts the old name.

Bird-Sounds-Global species (November 2026)

Until November 2026 the model knew only the 282 classes of the five datasets. The current model learned 351 more species from Bird-Sounds-Global. It was trained on spectrograms with the rolling 60 s noise floor and works with BirdBox's default floor as well (see Floor).

The previous model's classes keep their ids, so the species mapping Birds-With-Labels serves both models.

More on Birds-With-Labels:

  • Training: training curves and boxes per species and split.
  • Model Types: the export formats and how closely they match the PyTorch model.

docs.title: Precision, Recall and F1-Score
docs.text:
The graph below shows the performance of the model on the test splits under different confidence thresholds: precision, recall and the F1-score, each averaged over the species with test labels (macro average). The upper panel is the test split of the five datasets, the lower one the test split of Bird-Sounds-Global. To optimize the F1-score, pick a confidence threshold around 0.35. The demo starts at 0.25, which keeps more detections at a lower precision.

Average over the labelled species

The F-beta analysis (f_beta_score_analysis.py) also averages over species that have detections but no test labels, each with an F1 of 0 (Overall_Macro). A model with more classes has more of them, so this page averages over the labelled species only: 184 in the regional test split, 357 in Bird-Sounds-Global.

Starting at 0.05

The test detections were made at a confidence of 0.05, so the curves start there.

docs.title: Just-Bird Label Refinement
docs.text:
Most training datasets of the Just Bird model put one box around a whole song or bout, while the model should draw one box per call. Such boxes also cover the pauses between the calls. A study on crowd-sourced bird recordings found the same problem with labels that cover whole clips, and turned them into call-level labels [2]. Before training, those boxes are replaced by call boxes from a teacher model, in two rounds (see Training Recipe). This page explains the rule, what each round changes, which boxes and clips are discarded, and two changes that were tested: a looser rule for call-sized boxes, and removing nested boxes from the refined labels.

Most of the page describes the labels of the October 2026 model, made by teachers trained on PCEN spectrograms. The current model's labels were made the same way, with both changes and with teachers trained on log-floor spectrograms. The November 2026 Labels shows what that changes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The refinement changes only the four bout-labelled datasets: Northeastern US, Western US, Amazon Basin and Bird-Sounds-Global. Hawai'i and Southern Sierra Nevada keep their human call labels (Which Datasets Are Refined explains why). It works on the training images, 3 s clips that overlap by half. An annotation longer than a clip is cut into one box per clip, and each of these boxes is handled on its own.

Terms used on this page:

  • Human box: a box an annotator drew. In these four datasets it usually covers a whole song or bout of several seconds.
  • Replaced: the teacher found at least one call box for the human box, and those call boxes take its place. A human box can be replaced by many call boxes or by one.
  • Discarded: the teacher found no call box that qualifies (see the rule below), so the human box cannot be replaced. It is not used as the annotator drew it either: the human box and its whole 3 s clip are discarded from training, including any other boxes in that clip. Training on long bout boxes made the model worse on a new site (F1 0.122 against 0.380, see Each Step on the Unseen Site), so none is kept. Leaving out training samples whose labels cannot be trusted is a common way to learn from noisy labels (sample selection, [28]).
  • Call-sized: the whole annotation, before it was cut into clips, is at most 0.5 s long, the median length of the Hawai'i call labels. Here the annotator boxed a single call. Longer annotations cover a phrase, song or bout; they are 96% of the boxes in these four datasets.

docs.title: Which Datasets Are Refined
docs.text:
The datasets differ in what one human box covers. In each, every box was traced back to the whole annotation it was cut from (training split, boxes counted per 3 s clip):

Dataset What one box covers Median annotation length Boxes from call-sized annotations Refined Hawai'i a call 0.60 s 47% no Southern Sierra Nevada a call 0.40 s 55% no Bird-Sounds-Global mixed: calls, songs, bouts 2.08 s 7% yes Western US a bout 3.30 s 1% yes Northeastern US a bout 5.50 s 4% yes Amazon Basin a bout 12.80 s 1% yes

The annotation guidelines of Northeastern US, Western US and Amazon Basin let annotators join consecutive calls with pauses under 5 s into one box. The guidelines of Southern Sierra Nevada have no such clause, and Hawai'i is labelled per call as well. Bird-Sounds-Global, soundscapes from xeno-canto, mixes both styles; most of its boxes cover more than one call.

Hawai'i and Southern Sierra Nevada are left as they are, for four reasons:

  • There is nothing to split. About half of their boxes are call-sized, and the median annotation is at most 0.6 s. The rule exists to cut long bout boxes into calls.
  • The rule would lose good labels. A call box the teacher finds is replaced by about the same box, so nothing is gained. A call box the teacher misses is discarded with its whole clip, like the valid faint call below. On call-level labels the rule can only cost data.
  • Hawai'i defines what a call box is. Teacher 1 learned from the Hawai'i labels. Relabelling them with a model trained on them would only feed the teacher's own mistakes back into the training data.
  • Southern Sierra Nevada was the unseen test site while the recipe was developed (see Training Recipe). Its labels had to stay human to measure the teachers and models against. The released model adds them unchanged.

docs.title: The Rule
docs.text:
For every clip:

  1. The teacher proposes boxes with a confidence of at least 0.05. The cutoff is low on purpose: inside a box a human drew, even a weak detection is likely a call. Self-training for object detection usually keeps only confident boxes, because low-confidence boxes are often false positives and would become false labels anywhere in the image [15], [26]. Here the human box limits where a teacher box can go, so a weak box inside it is much less likely to be wrong.
  2. Half-inside test: a teacher box qualifies for a human box when at least half of the teacher box lies within the human box. Small call boxes inside a bout box pass easily.
  3. The qualifying teacher boxes replace the human box. They are trimmed to its edges, so a new box never leaves the time and frequency range the annotator marked.
  4. Near-duplicates (IoU ≥ 0.6, for example one call inside two overlapping human boxes) are merged, keeping the more confident box.
  5. If no teacher box qualifies, the human box is discarded, and with it the whole clip.

The test is measured on the teacher box, which makes it strict with tight call boxes. The teacher often draws a slightly larger box around the same call. Then less than half of the teacher box lies inside the tight human box (middle), so a good label is discarded with its clip. The looser rule on the right is tested in Testing a Looser Rule.

Real clips from the training data. All teacher boxes in the figure are from teacher 2, the second round, whose labels the released model was trained on:

In the first three clips the human box is replaced: a bout box by five call boxes, a call box that already fits its call by an almost identical box, and a loose call box by a tighter one. In the last three it is discarded with its clip, for the reasons in Why Boxes Are Discarded.

The last three clips, round by round:

  • Teacher boxes stick out (Western US): discarded in round 1 and in round 2.
  • Valid faint call (Northeastern US): the human box is correct, but discarded in round 1 and in round 2. Neither teacher finds the call, even with the confidence cutoff lowered from 0.05 to 0.001: no box of teacher 1 or teacher 2 even touches the human box. So the clip and its good label are lost to training. This is the price of the rule: a call that no teacher detects cannot be told apart from a stretch of silence inside a long annotation, and both are discarded.
  • Quiet stretch (Amazon Basin): replaced in round 1, where teacher 1 drew boxes in it, and discarded in round 2. It is one of the few clips that round 2 discards and round 1 kept (see the next section).

Two things the rule cannot do:

  • It never adds a label. A call outside every human box stays unlabelled, as in the original data.
  • A call the teacher misses inside a bout box loses its label, because the call boxes replace the whole bout box. In the bout clip above, the short, low sound at about 0.45 s gets no box in either round and now counts as background. A lower confidence cutoff would find more of these calls, but would also accept more noise.

docs.title: What Each Round Changes
docs.text:
Round 1 cuts the median box length from 1.15–3.0 s to 0.43–1.16 s, and round 2 to 0.38–0.82 s, close to the 0.50 s of the call-level Hawai'i labels. The larger effect of round 2 is that it replaces more of the bout boxes, so far fewer clips are discarded:

Dataset Training clips Discarded, round 1 Discarded, round 2 Used for training Northeastern US 116,780 25,847 (22%) 10,617 (9%) 106,163 Western US 36,435 13,605 (37%) 9,014 (25%) 27,421 Amazon Basin 31,264 23,730 (76%) 18,101 (58%) 13,163 Bird-Sounds-Global 84,404 23,826 (28%) 15,334 (18%) 69,070

Round 2 does not build on the labels of round 1. Both rounds start again from the original human boxes, so teacher 2 gets a new chance at every clip that round 1 discarded. Teacher 2 never trained on those clips (it was trained on the round-1 labels, without the discarded clips), but it learned from far more data than teacher 1, which saw only Hawai'i. Comparing the discarded clips of the two rounds:

Dataset Discarded, round 1 Kept again in round 2 Discarded in both rounds Kept in round 1, discarded in round 2 Northeastern US 25,847 15,433 10,414 203 Western US 13,605 4,668 8,937 77 Amazon Basin 23,730 5,795 17,935 166 Bird-Sounds-Global 23,826 8,938 14,888 446 All four 87,008 34,834 (40%) 52,174 892

Teacher 2 finds the calls in 40% of the clips that round 1 discarded. Only 892 clips go the other way. A call that neither teacher finds, like the faint call above, stays discarded.

docs.title: Why There Is No Third Round
docs.text:
A third round would train teacher 3 on the round-2 labels and relabel again. It was not run, because round 2 already brought no gain on full recordings of the unseen site:

Labels of the bout-labelled datasets F1 at IoU 0.5, unseen site, at the Hawai'i-val threshold Discarded clips Human boxes 0.122 none Round 1 0.380 87,008 Round 2 0.384 53,066
  • Round 1 brought the big step, from bout boxes to call boxes.
  • Round 2 ties round 1 on full recordings. Its gains lie elsewhere: 33,942 more clips are kept (19% more bout-labelled training data), 3 s clips score higher, and the threshold chosen on Hawai'i val carries over to the new site.
  • A third round could only win back clips from the 52,174 discarded in both rounds, many of them silent stretches of long annotations. Winning back 1,604 of them with the looser rule moved no score beyond what another training seed would.

A third round was not tested, so this is a judgment from the trend, not a measurement. Each round needs a new teacher, a relabelling of all four datasets and a final training to measure it.

Amazon Basin loses the most. Its recordings are dense choruses with long, overlapping annotations, and even after round 2 more than half of its clips are discarded.

docs.title: Why Boxes Are Discarded
docs.text:
A discarded box is not one the teacher judged to be correct: when the teacher finds the call in a good call box, it replaces it with about the same box (the second real clip above). A human box is discarded only when no teacher box passes the half-inside test, for one of two reasons:

  • No teacher box. The teacher finds nothing in the box. Usually this is a stretch of a long annotation where the bird is silent or barely audible in this clip, or a faint call.
  • The teacher box sticks out. Teacher boxes touch the human box, but less than half of each lies inside it. This happens where boxes of several birds overlap, as in the Amazon Basin choruses, and where the teacher draws a larger box around a call than the annotator did (the drawing above).

To see which boxes these are, every human box was traced back to the whole annotation it was cut from, and the teacher was run again on every clip with a discarded box:

Dataset Human boxes Call-sized Discarded, all boxes Discarded, call-sized Call-sized share of the discarded boxes Northeastern US 151,983 5,423 (3.6%) 7% 22% 11% Western US 54,951 316 (0.6%) 19% 70% 2% Amazon Basin 77,792 733 (0.9%) 34% 74% 2% Bird-Sounds-Global 125,370 8,467 (6.8%) 15% 31% 14% All four 410,096 14,939 (3.6%) 16% 31% 7%

Round 2, training split, boxes counted per 3 s clip.

  • Call-sized boxes are discarded more often than longer ones: 31% against 16% over all four datasets. In 62% of these cases the teacher did find something, but its box sticks out, as in the drawing.
  • But call-sized boxes are rare. These datasets were annotated per bout, and only 3.6% of their boxes are call-sized. They make up 7% of the discarded boxes.
  • Most discarded boxes come from long annotations. In 48% of them the teacher found nothing, mostly silent or faint stretches. In the rest its boxes stick out, above all in Amazon Basin (65% of its discarded boxes).

docs.title: Testing a Looser Rule for Call-Sized Boxes
docs.text:
Because the half-inside test rejects good call boxes whenever the teacher draws a larger box, a looser rule was tested on the same hold-out. For call-sized human boxes only, a teacher box also qualifies when it covers at least half of the human box. It is trimmed to the human box, so the label stays about the same as the annotator drew it, and the clip stays in training. In short: if the teacher confirms there is a call, the clip is kept.

This keeps 1,604 clips that the current rule discards, 0.6% more bout-labelled training data. A model trained with them, with the recipe otherwise unchanged, scores:

Rule Unseen site, IoU 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 Unseen site, IoU 0.5 at the Hawai'i-val threshold Hawai'i val, IoU 0.5 Current 0.541 / 0.384 / 0.116 0.383 0.584 Looser for call-sized boxes 0.541 / 0.389 / 0.120 0.387 0.586

Every score is the same or up to 0.005 higher, no more than a second training run with another seed moves it (0.001–0.006, see Nested Boxes). Discarding these clips costs nothing measurable, and keeping them does no harm: a manual check of some of the kept clips found real calls in the human boxes, with teacher boxes far larger than the call around them. The October model kept the current rule. The current model uses the looser one (--call-cover 0.5 in refine_coarse_boxes.py), together with dropping nested boxes (The November 2026 Labels).

docs.title: Nested Boxes in the Refined Labels
docs.text:
In the round-2 labels, about half of the boxes of the four refined datasets lie at least 80% inside a larger box of the same clip. Nearly all of these pairs (97–99.7%) lie inside one human box: teacher 2 often draws a phrase box and the syllable boxes inside it, both pass the half-inside test, and the merge in step 4 of the rule only catches near-duplicates (IoU ≥ 0.6), not a small box inside a large one. Window fusion removes nested boxes from the model's output, but the training labels keep them.

Dataset Boxes inside a larger box, human labels Round 2 Hawai'i 2% not refined Southern Sierra Nevada 1% not refined Northeastern US 13% 51% Western US 3% 57% Amazon Basin 26% 52% Bird-Sounds-Global 3% 57%

Training split, boxes counted per 3 s clip; a box counts when at least 80% of it lies inside a larger box.

Two variants apply the nested-box step of window fusion to the labels: drop inner keeps the larger box of each pair (50–57% of the boxes go), drop outer keeps the smaller ones (37–41% go). A model was trained on each with the recipe otherwise unchanged, and the current recipe was trained a second time with another seed to measure the noise of one run. Full recordings, window fusion as BirdBox runs it, phrase gap off:

Labels Unseen site, IoU 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 Hawai'i val, IoU 0.5 Round 2 (current) 0.541 / 0.384 / 0.116 0.584 Round 2, second seed 0.543 / 0.390 / 0.115 0.587 Drop inner 0.550 / 0.392 / 0.130 0.587 Drop outer 0.513 / 0.341 / 0.081 0.591
  • The second seed moves the scores by 0.001–0.006. Differences of that size are noise.
  • Drop inner gains most at IoU 0.75 (+0.014), where the fit of the box counts most.
  • Drop outer learns syllable fragments: on 3 s clips its median box is 0.19 s, against 0.24 s for round 2 and 0.40 s for the median annotation of the unseen site. Its confidences also fall on the unseen site, so a threshold chosen on Hawai'i val does not carry over.

docs.title: Measured on Calls as a User Wants Them
docs.text:
The unseen site's labels do not box one unit: some species are boxed per song element, others per phrase. Box F1 then penalises element boxes on a phrase label as much as a miss, so it cannot tell whether finer boxes are better. To measure that, 260 five-second stretches of the unseen site (21.7 min) were relabelled by hand by one person: missed calls added, phrase boxes split where the elements stand alone, and kept together where they only make sense together (458 boxes before, 567 after). F1 at IoU 0.5 on these labels, with a 95% interval from a paired bootstrap over the stretches:

Comparison Best threshold and phrase gap Defaults (threshold 0.15, phrase gap 0.05 s) Drop outer vs drop inner −0.010 [−0.054, +0.031] −0.092 [−0.147, −0.035] Drop inner vs round 2 +0.027 [−0.005, +0.059] +0.030 [−0.000, +0.059] Second seed vs round 2 +0.001 [−0.023, +0.025]
  • Finer boxes are not what is wanted. Drop outer's element boxes, joined by the phrase gap, match the hand labels slightly worse than drop inner, and at the default threshold clearly worse.
  • Drop inner is ahead of round 2 in every measurement, on the unseen site and on the hand labels, but never beyond the noise (on the hand labels just at its edge).

The October model kept the round-2 labels. The current model uses drop inner (make_nest.py inner) and the looser rule: both are cheap, and neither ever scored below round 2.

docs.title: The November 2026 Labels
docs.text:
The current model sees log-floor spectrograms, and so do its teachers: both were trained again on log-floor images, so the whole chain uses one kind of spectrogram. The rounds, the rule and their settings are the same as above, with the looser rule for call-sized boxes and drop inner. Teacher 1 kept epoch 27 of 50 (the PCEN teacher 1 kept epoch 24 of 44).

Training split, compared with the same rules run with the October (PCEN) teachers:

Dataset Clips used, PCEN teachers Clips used, log-floor teachers Boxes, PCEN teachers Boxes, log-floor teachers Median round-2 box, PCEN / log-floor Northeastern US 106,405 109,255 199,531 200,231 0.42 s / 0.48 s Western US 27,450 28,796 41,193 46,053 0.56 s / 0.51 s Amazon Basin 13,266 14,949 27,756 33,346 0.82 s / 0.84 s Bird-Sounds-Global 69,864 70,766 123,049 129,815 0.38 s / 0.38 s All four 216,985 223,766 391,529 409,445

Boxes are counted after drop inner. The log-floor teachers find a qualifying call box in more clips, so 6,781 fewer clips are discarded (3% more bout-labelled training data, most of it in Northeastern US and Amazon Basin), and the median box length barely changes.

A student was trained on each set of labels, on log-floor images and with the hold-out recipe, twice with different seeds. Full recordings of the unseen site, window fusion as BirdBox runs it, phrase gap off:

Teachers Unseen site, IoU 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 Unseen site, IoU 0.5 at the Hawai'i-val threshold Hand-labelled stretches, best F1 PCEN 0.549 / 0.392 / 0.128 0.389 0.462 PCEN, second seed 0.557 / 0.396 / 0.131 0.396 0.463 Log-floor 0.568 / 0.387 / 0.127 0.385 0.484 Log-floor, second seed 0.569 / 0.388 / 0.128 0.385 0.483
  • IoU 0.75 is a tie (−0.003 and −0.005, both within the noise), and IoU 0.25 is 0.012–0.019 higher with the log-floor teachers.
  • IoU 0.5 is slightly lower: −0.004 [−0.016, +0.007] and −0.011 [−0.021, −0.002] at the Hawai'i-val threshold. Against the October recipe (PCEN throughout), both seeds tie at IoU 0.5 (+0.002 and +0.003) and gain at IoU 0.75 (+0.009 and +0.007).
  • On the hand-labelled stretches both seeds score highest of all variants, +0.063 [+0.020, +0.107] over the October recipe.

The two log-floor seeds agree to within 0.001, while the two PCEN seeds differ by up to 0.008, so the IoU 0.5 gap is between 0.004 and 0.011. The log-floor teachers cost little, and in exchange no model in the chain depends on PCEN any more.

docs.title: Just-Bird Model Types and Format Parity
docs.text: BirdBox ships two pretrained models, Just-Bird and Birds-With-Labels. Both are released in multiple runtime formats to cover different deployment targets. This page covers the Just-Bird model. It documents every available format and shows how each one compares against the PyTorch baseline on identical recordings, so you can confirm that conversion or quantization does not degrade detection quality.

docs.title: Supported model formats
docs.text:
Each format targets a different deployment scenario. Install the matching runtime with python install.py --model-format <FORMAT>. See Installation for the full setup guide.

Format Typical use case Runtime .pt Default. PyTorch checkpoint, easiest to get started. PyTorch (CUDA or CPU) .onnx Cross-platform deployment, quantized variants available. ONNX Runtime (GPU or CPU) .tflite Edge devices and mobile targets. LiteRT / ai-edge-litert (CPU) .engine Maximum throughput on NVIDIA GPUs. TensorRT (NVIDIA GPU required)

Platform restrictions

.engine files are compiled for a specific GPU architecture. A model built on one card may not run on a different GPU generation.

Each format requires its own Python environment

Do not load a .tflite, .onnx, or .engine model from a .pt environment. The wrong environment will either raise an import error immediately or silently degrade results. Run python install.py --model-format <FORMAT> to install the correct runtime before switching formats. See Install Parameters for the full table.

docs.title: Verdict criteria
docs.text:
PASS

The model matches at least 90% of baseline detections, adds no more than 10% extra detections, and keeps the mean confidence difference at or below 0.05. The export is safe to use in place of the baseline.

WARN

One or more thresholds were exceeded. The model runs but performance may have degraded after conversion or quantization. Inspect the per-model detail below and compare detections on your own audio before deploying.

FAIL

The worker subprocess exited with an error. The model did not produce any detections. Check the per-model detail below for the full traceback.

docs.title: Metric glossary
docs.text:
Matching is one-to-one and recording by recording: a candidate detection can match a baseline detection of the same species when their 2D IoU (time and frequency) is at least 0.5. Pairs are taken in order of decreasing IoU, and each detection is used at most once.

Metric What it tells you Mean IoU Average time-and-frequency box overlap between matched pairs. 1.000 is a perfect overlap. Lower values mean boxes drifted in position or size. Mean Conf Δ Average absolute confidence difference on matched detections. Near 0.000 means the converted model is as confident as the baseline. Max Conf Δ Largest single confidence difference among matched detections. Surfaces worst-case outliers that the mean hides. Load (s) Wall-clock seconds to load the model file and build the detector. Detect (s) Wall-clock seconds spent running inference on all recordings.
